slides.sub: A slower trading week is a reason to follow up, not to wait.

captions.linkedin:
Qatar's weekly property trading slowed last week. That's not the moment for agencies to go quiet.

According to the Ministry of Justice weekly bulletin (reported by Gulf Times and QNA on 26 November), trading from 15 to 19 November exceeded QR377 million. Registered sale contracts came to about QR319 million, plus around QR58 million in residential unit sales. The week before (8–12 November), sale contracts were above QR564 million.

Why it matters:
Weekly numbers swing. One slower week says little about the market, and deals still closed across Al Wakrah, Doha, Al Rayyan, Lusail 69, The Pearl and more.

What agencies can do in a quieter week:
• Call back every lead that went cold this month
• Check that prices and details are current on every portal
• See which agents have unanswered leads
• Book viewings for buyers who were "just looking"

The buyers still active now deserve your full attention.

(Keeping every lead and listing in one place is why we built OneLinker CRM.)

How does your team use a slower week?
